attempts.summary: Joined node1, node2, and node3 (AlmaLinux 9.6) into a single RabbitMQ 4.2.9 cluster (installed from the CentOS Messaging SIG repo since rabbitmq.com was unreachable from the sandbox). Created the `payments` vhost with default_queue_type=quorum, and an `app_payments` application account with full configure/write/read permissions scoped to that vhost (management tag granted for HTTP API access; default `guest` account removed). Declared a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all 3 nodes, and demonstrated that durable messages survive the loss of any one node and remain fully consumable/publishable from the remaining two (verified twice, including cross-node produce-during-outage and consume-after-recovery cycles). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time OS reboot protocol for all three nodes, capturing boot-identity change via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, confirming RabbitMQ came back healthy, and confirming full cluster/quorum recovery (vhost, user, permissions, and queue data all intact, with leader failover working) before proceeding to the next node. A final round-trip publish/consume from a third node after all reboots confirmed complete data and cluster consistency. Note: this specific RabbitMQ RPM build was observed to lose Khepri cluster membership if only the systemd service (not the whole OS) is restarted; genuine OS reboots (used for the mandatory protocol) did not exhibit this and self-recovered correctly each time, which was verified directly rather than assumed.
